verses.25:28: يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰ لَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أَتَّخِذۡ فُلَانًا خَلِيلࣰ ا

meaning: The root فَلَنَ (falana) serves as a placeholder for any person. Ibn Fāris defines it as كناية عن كل أحد — a way of referring to anyone without naming them. فُلَان is "so-and-so", with فُلَانَة for a woman, and the shortened فُلُ occurring in verse.
en_note: Statistically derived from translation co-occurrence, not a lexical definition. Highlighting only.
meaning_previous: The root فُلَانٌ (fulān) refers to "such a one" or "so-and-so," used as a placeholder for a person's name, typically male. فُلَانَةٌ (fulānah) is its female equivalent.
meaning_source: Derived from the classical dictionaries (chiefly Maqayis al-Lugha, Ibn Faris d.1004) held in lexicon_full/
